payload.summary: Planned Phase 1 of the principal-credential-architecture roadmap: make agents.yaml canonical and derive all identity/trust projections (DB profiles, identity map, trust scale) from it, fail-loud for known agents. Roadmap (4 phases: registry canonical, per-agent OpenBao, session tokens, unified posture) created alongside the fully detailed pca-01 change. Approach 1 (startup sync, materialized-view DB) selected at Gate 1.

decisions.title: agent_profiles is a materialized view synced at startup
decisions.rationale: Explicit seeding was specced 2026-03 and never implemented across two shipped changes; operator-invoked consistency is the documented failure mode. Orphans disabled (never deleted) with audit events.

decisions.title: Transport does not gate identity generation
decisions.rationale: MCP agents reach the HTTP API via the proxy fallback, so every registry agent is an HTTP principal and gets an identity map entry.

decisions.title: Fail-loud scoped to registry-declared agents
decisions.rationale: Known agent with missing/disabled profile = hard error + audit event (projection machinery failed); unknown principals keep the low default (registry cannot be authoritative for principals it does not name).

decisions.title: One trust scale (0-4) in src/trust_levels.py
decisions.rationale: Adopts the names agent-coordinator already documents (Untrusted/Limited/Standard/Elevated/Admin); YAML schema 1-5 range was a bug; validators derive from the module.

decisions.title: AppRole retained; SPIFFE naming and authenticator seam adopted (roadmap-level)
decisions.rationale: Trust-anchor analysis: on a single-uid dev machine attestation carries no signal, so provisioner trust via wrapped single-use secret_ids is honest; SPIFFE IDs and JWT-SVID-shaped tokens keep SPIRE/OIDC adoptable when OpenShell k3s makes attestation real.

next_steps: Implement wp-contracts then wp-trust-scale first (/implement-feature derive-agent-identity-from-registry)
Planning lock claims were skipped 'unauthorized' by the live coordinator - itself an instance of the identity gap; re-register claims once implement-feature runs with a properly registered agent
